unknowns: The source-ingest PostgreSQL connector executes SELECT against operator-configured external allowlisted tables and information_schema.columns (src/core/source-ingest/connectors/postgres.ts:46-50,136-138). Those external relation names are dynamic and cannot be enumerated statically; its connector credential should be a separate read-only principal, not the GBrain runtime role.

SELECT on page_links and entity_pages views occurs in normal PostgresEngine queries. View-level GRANT requirements and underlying-table privilege behavior depend on view ownership/security_invoker settings; the underlying base-table commands visible in source are inventoried, but view ACLs are outside the requested table-command list.

Runtime reads page_generation_clock_seq via SELECT last_value and page writes invoke nextval through bump_page_generation_clock_fn. Exact least privilege therefore also needs sequence privileges (at least SELECT for last_value and USAGE/UPDATE as required for nextval), which are not expressible as SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE table commands.

Tables with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE were assigned UPDATE. PostgreSQL can additionally require column-level SELECT privileges for conflict expressions and RETURNING clauses; this inventory is table-command-level, not a column grant matrix.

Foreign-key, trigger, and cascade side effects generally execute through PostgreSQL internals or trigger routines and may introduce sequence EXECUTE/USAGE requirements. Cross-table routine access identified in source was noted, but function EXECUTE and sequence privileges are outside the output command vocabulary.

Optional subsystems (AI review, cycle/calibration, eval capture, source ingest, portal, and minions) are included because they are reachable through ordinary serve/MCP/CLI runtime. If a deployment disables one of these feature families, its table grants can be removed only after confirming the corresponding operations and background workers are unreachable.

The entries above distinguish core queue/source-ingest/autopilot/background paths, but deployment should also restrict claimable handler names if a narrower role is required.

Plugin handlers loaded from GBRAIN_PLUGIN_PATH at src/commands/jobs.ts:2106-2123 are not statically bounded by this repository. Their table access cannot be allowlisted without inspecting each deployed plugin.

The protected subagent handler can dispatch allowlisted brain operations. Its effective table access depends on the deployed BRAIN_TOOL_ALLOWLIST and submitted tool calls, so subagent-capable workers cannot be reduced to only the queue tables.
Routine autopilot table access is phase-dependent and schema-pack-dependent. Disabled phases do not require their conditional tables; custom schema-pack phases may add accesses not represented here.

Source connector implementations may read an external PostgreSQL database through a separate connector connection. Those external source tables are not GBrain runtime tables and require a separate, connector-specific SELECT-only allowlist.

Engine methods such as importFromContent, addLinksBatch, addTimelineEntriesBatch and page restore/delete encapsulate SQL in postgres-engine.ts. Their command sets were included where the call chain was explicit, but column-level grants and sequence USAGE requirements were outside this per-table command inventory.

INSERT privileges on serial/identity-backed tables may also require USAGE/SELECT on associated sequences depending on PostgreSQL identity configuration; sequence ACLs are not represented by the requested table-command schema.

Static repository inspection cannot establish current PostgreSQL owners, explicit/default ACLs, PUBLIC privileges, recursive role memberships, BYPASSRLS attributes, active RLS policies, or routine proconfig/search_path; no database queries were run.

The repository contains no SECURITY DEFINER runtime API or GRANT EXECUTE declarations for the recommended exclusions. Applying those exclusions now would break current persistent/admin/worker paths; exact replacement function names, argument types, return types, owners, search_path settings, and grants remain design work.

The intended process-role topology is not encoded here: serve-http combines OAuth, Portal, admin UI, request logging, connector configuration, and some scheduling, while source-ingest workers also need secret retrieval. Separate persistent, admin, and worker database identities would materially change the minimum ACL matrix.

It is unknown whether the legacy src/mcp/http-transport.ts bearer-token path is deployed. If it is, access_tokens SELECT/UPDATE and mcp_request_log INSERT remain mandatory until migrated to hardened routines.

It is unknown whether dynamic client registration is enabled in production. If disabled, normal persistent oauth_clients INSERT may be removable, although manual/admin client registration still requires a privileged path.
It is unknown whether the OAuth expiry sweep at serve-http.ts:634 is enabled in every deployment; when active it requires oauth_tokens and oauth_codes DELETE.

The config table mixes ordinary runtime knobs, worker checkpoints, authority controls, and at least one API-key-like value reference. PostgreSQL table ACL alone cannot safely grant writes by key namespace; the acceptable key-level mutation policy is not specified.

Portal trigger routines are SECURITY INVOKER and are integrity backstops only. Their current owner, EXECUTE ACL, and search_path posture cannot be proven statically, and they do not prevent callers with direct INSERT from forging portal_acl_audit attribution.

Secret retrieval currently returns decrypted credentials to application code. A hardened database routine can reduce table exposure but cannot eliminate credential exposure to the connector execution process; the intended connector-specific secret-broker boundary is unspecified.
